title: Tracking nonlinear solar-wind dynamics over three solar cycles using Wind observations
authors: Dario Javier Zamora, Facundo Maximo Abaca
abstract: The solar wind is a turbulent, weakly collisional plasma characterized by non-Gaussian fluctuations, long-range correlations, and multifractal dynamics. We investigate the long-term evolution of these properties using hourly proton density measurements obtained directly by the Wind spacecraft over 1995--2025. The use of a single-spacecraft dataset provides an independent test of previous results derived from the multi-spacecraft OMNI database. The three components of the nonextensive $q$-triplet are estimated within one-year sliding windows shifted monthly: $q_{stat}$ from the distribution of density increments, $q_{rel}$ from the decay of the autocorrelation function, and $q_{sens}$ from the multifractal spectrum. Their mean values, $q_{stat}=1.71\pm0.07$, $q_{rel}=4.62\pm0.52$, and $q_{sens}=-0.45\pm0.27$, confirm the persistent presence of heavy-tailed statistics, slow relaxation, and weakly chaotic multifractal dynamics. The parameters nevertheless exhibit distinct temporal variability and relationships with solar activity. The Fourier spectrum of $q_{stat}$ contains a dominant period of approximately $10.1$ years, while its correlation with the sunspot number is positive and moderate ($r=0.611$). Correlation and mutual-information analyses show that $q_{stat}$ is primarily associated with solar proxies, whereas $q_{sens}$ displays stronger relationships with geomagnetic indices and $q_{rel}$ exhibits weaker dependencies. An anomalous enhancement of $q_{stat}$ around 2004 coincides with a sequence of intense interplanetary disturbances, although possible effects related to Wind's orbital transition must also be considered. These findings demonstrate the robustness of the nonextensive description and show that the statistical and dynamical properties of solar wind proton density show evidence of modulation by solar activity.
summary: This research analyzes decades of solar wind proton density data to characterize its statistical and dynamical properties using nonextensive statistical mechanics. By calculating the q-triplet, the authors confirm persistent heavy-tailed fluctuations and slow relaxation. Crucially, they demonstrate that these plasma properties are modulated by the solar cycle, showing a strong periodicity linked to solar activity.
main_problem: To investigate the long-term evolution and solar cycle dependence of nonlinear statistical and dynamical properties of solar wind plasma.
main_result: The statistical properties, characterized by the q-triplet, confirm persistent heavy-tailed statistics and slow relaxation, showing modulation by solar activity with a dominant periodicity of $\sim 10.1$ years.
method: The study uses nonextensive statistical mechanics to estimate the q-triplet ($	ext{qstat}$, $	ext{qrel}$, $	ext{qsens}$) from hourly proton density measurements using sliding time windows.
model_or_system: The physical system is the turbulent, weakly collisional solar wind plasma, analyzed using the Wind spacecraft's proton density measurements over three decades (1995–2025). The analysis framework is nonextensive statistical mechanics.
key_observables: The q-triplet ($	ext{qstat}$, $	ext{qrel}$, $	ext{qsens}$), proton density increments, autocorrelation function decay, and multifractal spectrum.
important_parameters: Mean values: $	ext{qstat}=1.71\pm0.07$, $	ext{qrel}=4.62\pm0.52$, $	ext{qsens}=-0.45\pm0.27$. Key regimes include $q>1$ for heavy tails and slow relaxation.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on a single-spacecraft dataset (Wind) to provide an independent test, though potential orbital transition effects must be considered.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the temporal evolution of the three q-parameters, the correlation between $	ext{qstat}$ and sunspot number, and the Fourier power spectrum of $	ext{qstat}$ showing a dominant $\sim 10.1$-year peak.
paper_structure: The paper analyzes the time series of the q-triplet over 1995–2025, calculates correlations with solar/geomagnetic indices, and uses Fourier analysis to determine periodicity and modulation by solar activity.
why_interesting: The application of nonextensive statistics and multifractal analysis to space plasma dynamics provides a rigorous, non-equilibrium framework for characterizing turbulence and long-range correlations in astrophysical plasmas.
